log_text:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/session/store.py", line 28, in get_session

    raise ConnectionError(self._error_message(e))
redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to 10.0.3.45:6379. Connection refused.
root_cause: The client was configured with the primary node's IP instead of the ElastiCache primary endpoint DNS name; after an automatic failover the old IP stopped accepting connections.
fix: Use the primary endpoint DNS name, enable retry_on_timeout and health_check_interval=30 in the redis client, and add exponential-backoff retries.

title: Expired TLS certificate on internal payments gateway

root_cause: sendEmail() was called without await inside a forEach loop, so a transient DNS failure for the SMTP host became an unhandled rejection that terminated the Node 20 process.
fix: Replace forEach with for...of + await (or Promise.allSettled), wrap in try/catch with retry, and register a process-level 'unhandledRejection' logger.

title: Docker build fails: no space left on device in CI runner
log_text:
#12 [builder 5/8] RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
#12 41.22 ERROR: Could not install packages due to an OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
#12 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c pip install -r requirements.txt" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
------
failed to solve: failed to copy files: write /var/lib/docker/overlay2/l/abc/diff/usr/lib: no space left on device
root_cause: Self-hosted CI runner never pruned Docker build cache and dangling images; /var/lib/docker filled the 50GB disk.
fix: Added a nightly `docker system prune -af --filter until=72h` cron, enabled BuildKit cache limits, and alerting on runner disk usage > 80%.

title: Kafka consumer lag from rebalance storm
log_text:
2025-02-27 16:45:12,881 WARN  o.a.k.c.c.i.ConsumerCoordinator - [Consumer clientId=events-consumer-3, groupId=events] Offset commit failed on partition events-7 at offset 991823: The coordinator is not aware of this member.
org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.CommitFailedException: Commit cannot be completed since the group has already rebalanced and assigned the partitions to another member. This means that the time between subsequent calls to poll() was longer than the configured max.poll.interval.ms
root_cause: Batch processing per poll() took longer than max.poll.interval.ms (300s) after a slow downstream API, so consumers were repeatedly kicked from the group, causing a rebalance loop and growing lag.
fix: Reduce max.poll.records from 500 to 100, move the slow API call to an async bounded executor, and raise max.poll.interval.ms to 600000.

log_text:
2025-03-21T09:05:55Z ERROR report-exporter upload failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/exporter/upload.py", line 22, in upload_report
    s3.put_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=key, Body=body, ServerSideEncryption='aws:kms')
botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the PutObject operation: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/report-exporter-role/i-0abc is not authorized to perform: kms:GenerateDataKey on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/1a2b

title: Celery tasks stuck: broker visibility timeout too short
log_text:
[2025-02-02 11:00:04,551: WARNING/MainProcess] Received task transcode[5f2a9b] (already acknowledged? redelivered=True)
[2025-02-02 11:00:04,552: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-3] Task transcode[5f2a9b] started
[2025-02-02 11:00:04,552: ERROR/ForkPoolWorker-1] Task transcode[5f2a9b] raised unexpected: IntegrityError('duplicate key value violates unique constraint "renditions_video_id_profile_key"')
root_cause: Transcodes took longer than the Redis broker's 1h visibility_timeout, so unacknowledged tasks were redelivered to another worker and ran twice.
fix: Raise broker_transport_options visibility_timeout to 6h, use acks_late with idempotent upserts, and split long transcodes into chunks.

title: Health check flapping: liveness probe too aggressive on JVM startup
log_text:
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age                From     Message
  ----     ------     ----               ----     -------
  Warning  Unhealthy  2m (x9 over 4m)    kubelet  Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.1.4.22:8080/actuator/health": dial tcp 10.1.4.22:8080: connect: connection refused
  Normal   Killing    2m (x3 over 4m)    kubelet  Container catalog-service failed liveness probe, will be restarted
root_cause: Spring Boot took ~70s to start after adding a cache warm-up, but the liveness probe started at 30s with 3 failures allowed, so Kubernetes killed the pod before it was ready.
fix: Add a startupProbe (failureThreshold 30, periodSeconds 5) so liveness only begins after startup; point liveness at /actuator/health/liveness.

title: Postgres rejects connections: too many clients
log_text:
2025-05-02T08:00:12Z ERROR search-api startup failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/search/db.py", line 19, in connect
    conn = psycopg2.connect(DSN)
psycopg2.OperationalError: connection to server at "10.0.4.20", port 5432 failed: FATAL:  sorry, too many clients already
root_cause: Each of 30 pods opens a pool of 20 connections, exceeding Postgres max_connections=500 after a scale-out; new pods are refused at startup.
fix: Put PgBouncer (transaction pooling) in front of Postgres, cut per-pod pool_size to 5, and alert when connections exceed 80% of max_connections.

title: DynamoDB throttling from hot partition key
log_text:
2025-03-30T18:20:11Z ERROR events-ingest write failed after 10 retries
botocore.errorfactory.ProvisionedThroughputExceededException: An error occurred (ProvisionedThroughputExceededException) when calling the PutItem operation (reached max retries: 9): The level of configured provisioned throughput for the table was exceeded.
root_cause: The partition key was the event date, so all writes for the day hit one partition and exceeded its per-partition limit even though table-level capacity was available.
fix: Change the key to a high-cardinality value (e.g. tenant_id#date with a shard suffix), switch to on-demand capacity during the migration, and watch the ThrottledRequests metric.

title: pytest: test database is being accessed by other users
error_type: OperationalError: database is being accessed by other users
log_text:
ERROR tests/conftest.py::django_db_setup - django.db.utils.OperationalError: database "test_accounts" is being accessed by other users
DETAIL:  There are 2 other sessions using the database.
=========================== short test summary info ============================
ERROR tests/test_signup.py::test_creates_user
1 error, 0 passed in 41.02s
root_cause: A background thread started by the app (a metrics flusher) held DB connections open past test teardown, so the test runner couldn't drop and recreate the test database.
fix: Stop background threads in a session-scoped fixture, close connections with django.db.connections.close_all() in teardown, and disable the flusher under settings.TESTING.

title: Celery WorkerLostError: worker killed by SIGKILL
log_text:
[2025-03-12 09:41:07,229: ERROR/MainProcess] Process 'ForkPoolWorker-2' pid:84 exited with 'signal 9 (SIGKILL)'
[2025-03-12 09:41:07,251: ERROR/MainProcess] Task handler raised error: WorkerLostError('Worker exited prematurely: signal 9 (SIGKILL) Job: 412.')
billiard.exceptions.WorkerLostError: Worker exited prematurely: signal 9 (SIGKILL) Job: 412.
root_cause: Concurrency 4 workers each loaded a full 4K video into memory; together they exceeded the container memory limit and the kernel OOM killer sent SIGKILL to a pool process.
fix: Stream frames instead of loading whole files, lower --concurrency to 2 for the heavy queue, set worker_max_memory_per_child, and size the container limit from measured peak.

title: Temporary failure in name resolution under load (CoreDNS)
error_type: socket.gaierror: Temporary failure in name resolution
log_text:
2025-04-22T16:05:51Z ERROR rate-limiter upstream lookup failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/socket.py", line 962, in getaddrinfo
    for res in _socket.getaddrinfo(host, port, family, type, proto, flags):
socket.gaierror: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution
  host=api.partner.example.com
root_cause: With the Kubernetes default ndots:5, every external lookup tried four search-domain suffixes first, multiplying DNS queries; under peak load CoreDNS was CPU-throttled and dropped queries.
fix: Set dnsConfig ndots: 2 (or use fully-qualified names with a trailing dot), scale CoreDNS and enable NodeLocal DNSCache, and raise CoreDNS CPU limits.

title: Alembic upgrade fails: multiple head revisions
log_text:
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Context impl PostgresqlImpl.
ERROR [alembic.util.messaging] Multiple head revisions are present for given argument 'head'; please specify a specific target revision, '<branchname>@head' to narrow to a specific head, or 'heads' for all heads
FAILED: Multiple head revisions are present for given argument 'head'
root_cause: Two feature branches each added a migration with the same down_revision; after both merged, the migration graph had two heads and the deploy's `alembic upgrade head` refused to run.
fix: Create a merge revision (`alembic merge heads -m 'merge'`), and add a CI check that fails when `alembic heads` returns more than one revision.
